cars.specification_market: Original early Bearcat production-road family, selected 1914 Series E / Model 4-E at Stahls. All seven attributes use the custodian's explicit technical table. Retain quoted 389.9 CID and 34x4 1/2-inch tyre notation without extra precision, rim-size assumptions or modern equivalents. No horsepower, rpm, torque, performance or mass is imported. Wisconsin engine data are not mixed with later Stutz-built engines, six-cylinder conversions, dedicated White Squadron racers, 1923 Henry Ford museum figures or later DV32 revivals. Family chronology is context; 1914 is the selected reference year, not a claimed start date. Road identity follows museum classification as a sporting road car. The museum and photograph identify the example but do not establish matching numbers, factory-original bodywork or an uninterrupted provenance. Group original years, engines, chassis and bodies once.
cars.summary: The original Stutz Bearcat is an enduring early American sports-car icon, built around minimal road bodywork and a rear transaxle, with a strong connection to Indianapolis performance culture. Its place in sporting-car history is supported by independent museum accounts and marque-club history. Count the original Bearcat road family once across years, engines and bodies; later revivals, replicas and cosmetic changes create no extra record here.
